declared.title: Self-efficacy, personal autonomy, life arrangements, and health priorities/preferences in psychological distress: a predictive, variance-based PLS-SEM structural model
declared.foundIn: rapport contre-preuve reports/too-many-choices/counter-evidence.md (2026-11-22), DOI trouvé par ses requêtes ; titre relevé sur Crossref par la session : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: 328 Arabic-speaking adults aged 18-65 (authors in Saudi Arabia and Egypt; country of the sample not given in the abstract)

findings.text: In an Arab sample, the link between self-efficacy and lower distress ran through a stronger sense of personal autonomy

support.sentence: Autonomy mediated self-efficacy's protective effect against distress (indirect β = -0.17, p < .001), while health priorities unexpectedly increased distress (β = 0.35, p < .001).

limits: cross-sectional structural model: no causal order
personal autonomy, not freedom of choice nor number of options
country of the sample not stated in the abstract
